22. // User Frame
23. //==================================================================================================
24. 
25. ///
26. /// # Description
27. ///
28. /// A type that represents a user frame.
29. ///
30. #[derive(Debug)]
31. #[verus_verify(external_derive)]
32. pub struct UserFrame {
33.     /// Frame address.
34.     addr: FrameAddress,
35. }
36.

38. verus! {
39. 
40. use crate::hal::mem::spec_page_size;
41. use crate::mm::phys::FrameAllocView;
42. 
43. /// Abstract view of a user frame: the physical address of the owned frame.
44. impl View for UserFrame {
45.     type V = int;
46. 
47.     closed spec fn view(&self) -> int {
48.         self.addr@
49.     }
50. }
51. 
52. /// Abstract view of the user page pool: the frame partition it draws from.
53. ///
54. /// The pool carries no spec-readable state of its own — its real state is the global frame
55. /// allocator — so its view is uninterpreted. The cross-call transition is realized by the
56. /// proving-phase ghost token over the singleton allocator; the trust obligation for the two
57. /// state-affecting operations is tracked by `Upool::new`/`Upool::alloc` being `external_body`.
58. impl View for Upool {
59.     type V = FrameAllocView;
60. 
61.     uninterp spec fn view(&self) -> FrameAllocView;
62. }
63. 
64. } // verus!
65. 
66. #[verus_verify]
67. impl UserFrame {
68.     ///
69.     /// # Description
70.     ///
71.     /// Instantiates a user frame.
72.     ///
73.     /// # Parameters
74.     ///
75.     /// - `addr`: Frame address.
76.     ///
77.     /// # Returns
78.     ///
79.     /// A user frame.
80.     ///
81.     #[verus_spec(result =>
82.         requires
83.             addr.inv(),
84.         ensures
85.             result@ == addr@,
86.             result.inv(),
87.     )]
88.     pub fn new(addr: FrameAddress) -> Self {
89.         Self { addr }
90.     }
91. 
92.     ///
93.     /// # Description
94.     ///
95.     /// Returns the physical address of the target user frame.
96.     ///
97.     /// # Returns
98.     ///
99.     /// The physical address of the target user frame.
100.     ///
101.     #[verus_spec(result =>
102.         requires
103.             self.inv(),
104.         ensures
105.             result@ == self@,
106.             result.inv(),
107.     )]
108.     pub fn address(&self) -> FrameAddress {
109.         self.addr
110.     }
111. 
112.     ///
113.     /// # Description
114.     ///
115.     /// Consumes the user frame without freeing the underlying physical frame.
116.     ///
117.     /// # Returns
118.     ///
119.     /// The frame address.
120.     ///
121.     #[verus_spec(result =>
122.         requires
123.             self.inv(),
124.         ensures
125.             result@ == self@,
126.             result.inv(),
127.     )]
128.     pub fn leak(self) -> FrameAddress {
129.         let this: ManuallyDrop<Self> = ManuallyDrop::new(self);
130.         this.addr
131.     }
132. 
133.     ///
134.     /// # Description
135.     ///
136.     /// Adds a new reference to the underlying physical frame and returns a fresh
137.     /// [`UserFrame`] handle that owns that reference. The two handles share the
138.     /// same physical frame, and the frame is only reclaimed once both handles are
139.     /// dropped.
140.     ///
141.     /// This is the building block for copy-on-write sharing: the parent retains
142.     /// its handle, the child receives the returned handle.
143.     ///
144.     /// # Returns
145.     ///
146.     /// On success, a new [`UserFrame`] that aliases the same physical frame as
147.     /// `self`. On failure, an error is returned.
148.     ///
149.     #[verus_spec(result =>
150.         requires
151.             self.inv(),
152.         ensures
153.             match result {
154.                 Ok(uf) => {
155.                     &&& uf@ == self@
156.                     &&& uf.inv()
157.                     &&& crate::mm::phys::phys_view().frames.is_allocated(self@)
158.                 },
159.                 Err(_) => {
160.                     ||| !crate::mm::phys::phys_view().frames.is_allocated(self@)
161.                     ||| crate::mm::phys::phys_view().frames.refcounts[self@] >= 255
162.                 },
163.             },
164.     )]
165.     pub fn share(&self) -> Result<UserFrame, Error> {
166.         frame::share(self.addr)?;
167.         Ok(Self { addr: self.addr })
168.     }
169. 
170.     ///
171.     /// # Description
172.     ///
173.     /// Returns the current reference count of the underlying physical frame.
174.     ///
175.     /// # Returns
176.     ///
177.     /// Upon success, the current reference count of the underlying physical frame is returned.
178.     /// Upon failure, an error is returned instead.
179.     ///
180.     #[verus_spec(result =>
181.         requires
182.             self.inv(),
183.         ensures
184.             match result {
185.                 Ok(count) => {
186.                     &&& crate::mm::phys::phys_view().frames.is_allocated(self@)
187.                     &&& count as int == crate::mm::phys::phys_view().frames.refcounts[self@]
188.                 },
189.                 Err(_) => !crate::mm::phys::phys_view().frames.is_allocated(self@),
190.             },
191.     )]

194.     }
195. }

201.         no_unwind

233.     /// Instantiates a user frame pool.
234.     ///
235.     /// # Returns
236.     ///
237.     /// A user frame pool.
238.     ///

241.     // uninterpreted `View for Upool` and cannot be discharged from the empty struct body (the

246.     #[verus_verify(external_body)]
247.     #[verus_spec(result =>
248.         ensures
249.             result@.wf(),
250.     )]

252.         Self { _private: () }

257.     ///
258.     /// Allocates a single user frame from the user frame pool.

262.     /// Upon success, a user frame is returned. Upon failure, an error is returned instead.

271.     // `verus-ai-logs/nanvix-phys-phys-upool/verification_todo.md`.
272.     #[verus_verify(external_body)]
273.     #[verus_spec(result =>
274.         requires
275.             old(self)@.wf(),
276.         ensures
277.             final(self)@.wf(),
278.             match result {
279.                 Ok(uf) => {
280.                     &&& old(self)@.is_free(uf@)
281.                     &&& final(self)@ == old(self)@.alloc_one(uf@)
282.                 },
283.                 Err(_) => {
284.                     &&& final(self)@ == old(self)@
285.                     &&& old(self)@.free_count() == 0
286.                 },
287.             },

6. # Proof Extraction
7. 
8. Extract large inline `proof { ... }` blocks from exec code into named lemmas
9. in the proof file (`<module>.proof.rs`).
10. 
11. ## Why
12. 
13. Large inline proof blocks hurt readability and make exec code hard to review.
14. Extracting them into lemmas with clear names documents *what* is being proven
15. and makes proofs reusable.
16.

18.

20. 
21. ```bash
22. python3 scripts/check_proof_blocks.py <source_file> --threshold 5 --all
23. ```
24. 
25. Output shows each proof block with its enclosing function, line range, and size.
26. Blocks marked `⚠️ EXTRACT` exceed the threshold.
27. 
28. ## Rules
29. 
30. | Block size  | Action |
31. |-------------|--------|
32. | >5 lines    | **Must** extract into a lemma in `.proof.rs` |
33. | 4-5 lines   | Extract if generic/reusable; keep if tightly coupled to exec context |
34. | 1-3 lines   | Keep inline |
35. 
36. ## Extraction Process
37. 
38. For each block to extract:
39. 
40. 1. Read the proof block and identify what it proves (the key `assert` / property).
41. 2. Create `proof fn lemma_<descriptive_name>` in `.proof.rs` with:
42.    - `requires`: the preconditions the proof depends on
43.    - `ensures`: the property being proven (must be strong enough for the call site)
44. 3. Replace the inline block with a 1-3 line lemma call.
45. 4. Run verification to confirm it still passes.
46.

58.         forall|j: int| 0 <= j < i ==> result[j] == f(input[j]),
59.         ... // 7 more clauses
60. { ... }
61. 
62. // After: grouped into named predicates
63. spec fn loop_partial_result_ok(result: Seq<T>, input: Seq<T>, i: int) -> bool {
64.     result.len() == i
65.     && forall|j: int| 0 <= j < i ==> result[j] == f(input[j])
66. }
67. 
68. while i < n
69.     invariant
70.         0 <= i <= n,
71.         loop_partial_result_ok(result@, input@, i as int),
72.         ... // remaining clauses
73. { ... }
74. ```

86.

3. description: "Remove redundant proof artifacts (assertions, lemmas, hints, dead code) without weakening guarantees. Use when polishing verified code to reduce verbosity."

5. 
6. # Proof Minimization
7. 
8. Remove redundant proof artifacts to make verification lean and readable
9. without weakening any guarantees.
10. 
11. ## What to Remove
12. 
13. 1. **Redundant lemmas** — another lemma proves the exact same property
14.    (same `requires` AND same `ensures`).
15. 2. **Redundant assertions** — `assert` statements that Verus can verify
16.    without them. Remove in bulk, then re-run verification.
17. 3. **Redundant proof hints** — unnecessary `by`, `by(nonlinear_arith)`,
18.    or trigger annotations that Verus doesn't need.
19. 4. **Dead spec functions** — non-public spec functions with zero callers (not
20.    referenced in any `requires`, `ensures`, `invariant`, or lemma). Keep
21.    `pub` spec functions — they may be part of the module's API for dependents.
22. 5. **Debug artifacts** — In spec/proof files: remove TODO comments, commented-out
23.    code, and property-ID annotations (e.g., `// FUNC-POST-3`, `// INV-2`). In
24.    exec files: remove unnecessary verification-related comments (e.g., obsolete
25.    proof hints, property-ID tags); do NOT remove original source comments.
26. 
27. ## What is NOT Redundant
28. 
29. - **Uncalled lemmas**: Verus verifies all lemmas regardless of callers.
30.   An uncalled lemma still proves a property. Only remove if another lemma
31.   proves the *exact* same thing.
32. - **Different preconditions**: Two lemmas with different `requires` prove
33.   different properties even if `ensures` looks similar.
34. 
35. **When in doubt, keep it.**
36. 
37. ## Process
38. 
39. This is a best-effort pass for readability, not an exhaustive search.
40. 
41. 1. **Assertions**: Remove `assert` statements that look redundant based on context.
42. 2. **Lemmas**: Remove a lemma only if another has identical `requires` + `ensures`.
43. 3. **Proof hints**: Remove `by(...)` annotations that look unnecessary.
44. 4. Re-run verification after changes — if it fails, revert the removal.
45. 
46. ## Constraints
47. 
48. - Do NOT add `assume`, `admit`, or `external_body`.
49. - Do NOT weaken any `ensures` or remove any meaningful property.
50. - Verification must pass after every removal batch.
51.
